title: Pick the right tier
scenario: You must review a 30-page vendor contract against five constraints — penalties, renewal, jurisdiction, data terms, deadlines. A missed clause has real financial consequences. Budget matters, but the review must be thorough.

options.text: Use the fastest, cheapest tier for everything to keep the cost down.
options.feedback: Cost control is real, but a missed clause costs far more than the tokens saved. This task is exactly where deliberation pays.

options.text: Use a reasoning tier for the conflict analysis, and keep clause extraction on a fast pass.
options.feedback: Yes — split by task shape: pattern extraction is fast-tier work; constraint checking and conflicts are reasoning work. Escalate where it matters, stay efficient everywhere else.

options.text: Use the fast tier but add “be very careful and thorough” to the prompt.
options.feedback: Instructions do not add thinking time. The carefulness you want is computation — and that is what the reasoning tier is for.

options.text: Use the flagship tier for every step and every document, always.
options.feedback: Overkill as a default: far more expensive and slower for work a fast pass does equally well. Reserve the top tier for what needs it.

hints: Split the job: which half is pattern work, which half is judgement?
explanation: Reasoning tiers buy deliberation with time and money; fast tiers win on one-pass transformations. The durable pattern: fast for extraction and volume, reasoning for multi-constraint judgement — and verify either way.
